I don't feel that there is any difference between the trolley scenario and the fat man. The intent is to save 5 people at the cost of killing one. Just because you push the fat man doesn't make it any worse than pulling the lever and killing the trolley man. You're still knowingly killing one person to save others. The action of pulling the lever is deliberate, and done knowing it will kill a person. The action of pushing a man off a bridge to cause the same effect as switching tracks is identical and I don't really understand why people think it's different. Both are a choice between inaction, allowing 5 people to die and one to live, or stepping in and changing the course of the trolley through a deliberate action to save the lives of 5 people while knowingly killing one.

Interestingly, when buddhist monks were asked this question, they too would throw the fat man on the tracks, primarily because they reasoned that the loss of life of 5 was greater than the loss of life of 1...even if you had to actively push the fat man on the tracks to save the 5 (and these monks are generally considered nonviolent). The thing is though, that doing nothing was also considered an action. So whether you pushed the fat man or didn't push the fat man, you were taking an action...one which would either kill 1 man, or another which would kill 5 men.
